messages:
maria: Heads up — after last night's KMS key rotation + RBAC role rename, multiple customers report SSO failures and SCIM deprovisioning flapping. Need immediate triage.

sanjay: Can you paste the error users are seeing? Any common IdP?

maria: Mostly Azure AD and Okta. Error from authproxy logs: 
```
2026-03-23T02:14:11Z authproxy ERROR saml: decryptAssertion: KMSDecryptFailed: InvalidCiphertextException
user=acct-123 extid=U:abcd1234
```

jen: That InvalidCiphertextException usually means the envelope key context doesn't match what's in KMS. Did the key alias change or rewrap happen?

maria: Yes — ops ran a rewrap rolling job at 01:40 and also applied the RBAC rename for `org:admin` -> `org:admin_v2` in the same maintenance window. ops-bot shows deploy completed.

ops-bot: deploy/redwood-identity-2026-03-23 completed by @ops at 01:42 UTC :white_check_mark:

dmitri: Two moving pieces is the problem. If the KMS rewrap changed the encryption context used for SCIM/JWE envelopes, decryption will fail and downstream code might drop the audit event if it can't parse the assertion.

maria: Confirmed — some deprov logs are missing the assertion id and we can't correlate to RBAC role pruning. Auditstore shows no deprov events for those externalIds.

sanjay: Action plan: 1) stop the rolling rewrap 2) try to decrypt a sample payload with the old key context 3) if successful, rewrap back or re-import old alias mapping.

jen: Also we need to check for any exploit window — if assertion parsing failed, did any code fall back to a permissive path? We must be sure no elevation occurred.

sec-oncall: Oncall here. Running quick audit: grep for missing deprov in auditstore between 01:40-02:10 UTC. If we see failed decrypts but no deny events, escalate.

maria: I grabbed a raw SAML assertion from logs (base64) and attempted local decrypt against the new key context => failed. I then submitted to KMS ops and got the last key version metadata: 
```
KeyId: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/aaa-bbb-ccc
LastRewrap: 2026-03-23T01:41:12Z
EncryptionContext: {"env":"prod","service":"authproxy","wrap_id":"wrap-20260323-01"}
```

dmitri: Our previous envelope context used wrap_id `wrap-20260322-99` — mismatch. That explains InvalidCiphertextException.

jen: Could SCIM deprovisioner have retried with a no-assertion path and ended up pruning wrongly? We have a known bug where if assertion parse fails the deprov worker marks the account stale but doesn't emit an audit event. That's CVE-not-related but serious for compliance.

maria: I have one repro where a user got deprovisioned but the audit log had no entry — customers are rightly upset.

sec-oncall: Immediate steps: (a) pause SCIM deprovisioner queue (b) halt further rewraps (c) restore previous key alias mapping if available (d) open incident and notify affected accounts.

ops-bot: Queue/scim-deprov paused by @ops at 02:03 UTC

sanjay: If we restore the old key mapping, existing envelopes should decrypt. Is the old wrapping key still available? ops, are backups/old key versions present?

maria: KMS shows previous key version ID `v23` still present, not scheduled for deletion. We can temporarily map alias redwood/kms-wrap -> v23. But need approval for rollback window.

dmitri: We also need to mitigate RBAC rename fallout. Any cached sessions referencing `org:admin` may have been invalidated or mismapped. That explains some 403s. We should implement a compatibility shim that accepts old role name for 24h.

jen: For compliance: capture a list of all accounts deprovisioned between 01:40-02:10 and run an immediate re-provision where possible, plus audit backfill once we restore decryption.

sec-oncall: Opening SEV-2 incident: INC-2026-0423. Notifying customers and compliance. Assigning owners: ops for KMS rollback, eng-identity for shim, security for audit/backfill and vuln triage.

maria: Running decryption test after alias remap... if successful I'll start replaying SCIM events into a dry-run consumer to generate audit events without mutating state.

sanjay: Also check for any CVE/upgrade that might have changed encryption context semantics in the KMS SDK used by authproxy. Could be a library upgrade that changed how context is serialized.

dmitri: Good point — authproxy released 1.12.0 two days ago with KMS SDK bump. I'll diff vendor/aws-kms between 1.11.x and 1.12.0.

maria: Quick status update: remapped alias to v23 at 02:22 UTC, sample assertion decrypts now succeed. Dry-run consumer shows 18 deprov events that previously had no audit lines. Will not apply changes until we confirm no unintended side-effects.

sec-oncall: Great. Next steps: 1) backfill auditstore with the 18 events, 2) restore SCIM queue to paused state until backfill validation done, 3) prepare customer-facing timeline and RCA draft, 4) schedule postmortem and fix for the deprov bug (ensure parse failures always emit audit deny events).

jen: Put a guard in code: if assertion parse fails -> emit explicit AuditEvent{type:deprov_failed, reason:decrypt_error, assertion_id:unknown, extid:provided} so compliance has traceability.

maria: Thanks team. I'll handle backfill and start drafting timeline. If anything changes I'll ping here. :phone: 

ops-bot: incident/INC-2026-0423 created and paging for oncall escalation.

sanjay: Also create a follow-up to add an integration test covering KMS rewrap + SDK upgrade matrix to prevent regression.

maria: Will add to eng-security retro and schedule the postmortem doc.

sec-oncall: Closing interim update. Leaving incident open until backfill verified.
